tool.name: Merge SAFRAN and ERA5 climate data
tool.description: combine matching site/date records from both files into one table
tool.command: python '$__tool_directory__/merge_safran_era5.py' --safran-file '$safran_input' --safran-site-column '$safran_site_column' --safran-date-column '$safran_date_column' #if $safran_value_columns --safran-value-columns '$safran_value_columns' #end if --era5-file '$era5_input' --era5-site-column '$era5_site_column' --era5-date-column '$era5_date_column' #if $era5_value_columns --era5-value-columns '$era5_value_columns' #end if --join-type '$join_type' --round-decimals '$round_decimals' #if str($date_start).strip() --date-start '$date_start' #end if #if str($date_end).strip() --date-end '$date_end' #end if --output '$merged_output'

param.name: safran_input
param.label: SAFRAN climate data file
param.help: Daily SAFRAN file with a site column, a date column and one or more climate variable columns, e.g. the output of the 'Get SAFRAN data (GEOSAS API)' tool.

param.name: safran_site_column
param.label: Site column (SAFRAN file)
param.help: Column identifying the site/location in the SAFRAN file.

param.name: safran_date_column
param.label: Date column (SAFRAN file)
param.help: Column holding the date in the SAFRAN file.

param.name: safran_value_columns
param.label: SAFRAN variable columns to keep
param.help: Climate variable columns to carry over from the SAFRAN file (e.g. T_Q, PRELIQ_Q). Leave empty to keep every column except the site and date columns.

param.name: era5_input
param.label: ERA5 climate data file
param.help: Daily ERA5 / ERA5-Land file with a site column, a date column and one or more climate variable columns, for the same sites as the SAFRAN file.

param.name: era5_site_column
param.label: Site column (ERA5 file)
param.help: Column identifying the site/location in the ERA5 file.

param.name: era5_date_column
param.label: Date column (ERA5 file)
param.help: Column holding the date in the ERA5 file.

param.name: era5_value_columns
param.label: ERA5 variable columns to keep
param.help: Climate variable columns to carry over from the ERA5 file (e.g. temperature_2m_mean, soil_moisture_0_to_7cm_mean). Leave empty to keep every column except the site and date columns.

param.name: join_type
param.label: How to combine records between the two files
param.help: Inner keeps only matching site/date pairs; left/right keep every record from one file and leave the other side's columns empty where there is no match; outer keeps every record from either file.
param.option: Inner join - keep only site/date combinations present in both files
Left join - keep every SAFRAN record
Right join - keep every ERA5 record
Outer join - keep every record from either file

param.name: date_start
param.label: Keep records on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD)
param.help: Leave empty to keep every date.

param.name: date_end
param.label: Keep records on or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD)
param.help: Leave empty to keep every date.

param.name: round_decimals
param.label: Decimal places for numeric columns
param.help: Number of decimal places used to round numeric columns (including any coordinate columns carried over) in the merged output.

data.name: merged_output
data.label: Merge SAFRAN & ERA5 climate data (${join_type} join) on ${on_string}

tool.help:
**What it does**
This tool combines a SAFRAN climate reanalysis file (for example, produced by the *Get SAFRAN data (GEOSAS API)* tool, covering metropolitan France) and an ERA5 / ERA5-Land reanalysis file for the same sites into a single table, matched on a site identifier and a date.
It is typically used to complete SAFRAN atmospheric variables (temperature, precipitation, potential evapotranspiration, ...) with ERA5 variables that SAFRAN does not provide, such as depth-resolved soil moisture and soil temperature, for the same site and date.
**Input format**
Both input files must be CSV files with a header row, each containing at least:
- a column identifying the site (e.g. ``site_name``) - a column holding the date (ideally ``YYYY-MM-DD``; other common date formats are also accepted and normalised to ``YYYY-MM-DD``) - one or more climate variable columns
The two files do not need to share the same column names, order, or set of sites: you choose which column plays each role, separately for each file.
**Joining records**
- *Inner*: keep only the site/date combinations present in **both** files. - *Left*: keep every SAFRAN record; ERA5 columns are left empty where there is no matching ERA5 record. - *Right*: keep every ERA5 record; SAFRAN columns are left empty where there is no matching SAFRAN record. - *Outer*: keep every record from either file.
If a variable column has the same name in both files, ``_safran`` and ``_era5`` suffixes are added so both are kept and can be told apart.
The exception is ``longitude`` and ``latitude``: when both files carry them, they are merged into a single ``longitude`` and a single ``latitude`` column. The SAFRAN value is kept (the ERA5 value is used only where there is no SAFRAN record), and a warning is logged if the two sources disagree.
**Output**
A single CSV file with ``site_name``, ``date``, and the selected climate variable columns from both sources, sorted by site and then date. Numeric columns are rounded to the chosen number of decimal places.
**Known limitations**
- Each site/date combination must be unique within each input file; the tool stops with an error if duplicates are found, rather than guessing which row to keep. - Dates that cannot be parsed cause the tool to stop with an error rather than being silently dropped. - SAFRAN covers metropolitan France only; sites outside that domain will only have ERA5 data, which matters for the *right* and *outer* join modes (the SAFRAN columns will be empty for those sites).
